page: OVHcloud b3-64 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC processor architecture running on a KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration integrates 400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and includes a baseline network interface provisioned at 4 Gbps, operating without bundled graphics processing units.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory subsystem and decompression throughput. In synthetic memory testing, the instance achieved 217.29 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 106.68 GB/sec for large-block writes, both ranking in the upper 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 214.59 GB/sec, complemented by a solid single-core stress-ng rating of 3078.58. Multi-core compute performance sits firmly in the middle 50 percent, recorded by a PassMark CPU score of 37,372.32 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 13,001.0.

The inclusion of dedicated non-hyperthreaded CPU cores combined with direct-attached NVMe storage yields predictable performance and eliminates noisy-neighbor variance on compute and disk I/O. Lacking hardware vector enhancements like AVX-512 or AMX, and with no dedicated GPU acceleration, the server is less suited for large matrix operations or intensive deep learning. Instead, the hardware balance makes OVHcloud b3-64 a cost-effective choice for relational databases, Redis caching layers, web application clusters, continuous integration workers, and container orchestration nodes.
description: OVHcloud b3-64 is a balanced general-purpose virtual instance based on the AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture. Delivered via the KVM hypervisor, it features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz, 64.0 GB of system memory, and 400 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. The machine includes a 4 Gbps network bandwidth baseline and does not incorporate dedicated GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate exceptional memory bandwidth, exceeding 217 GB/sec on uncached reads, along with strong single-core and multi-threaded decompression throughput. Standard processing metrics remain balanced, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,001.0. With its balanced 1:4 memory allocation and reliable local NVMe disk array, this server provides predictable performance and resource efficiency for enterprise databases, caching layers, container clusters, and distributed build pipelines.
